_comment: Placeholders / refs with no producer, each traced to a cause. NOT listed here = build fails.

accepted_dollar_refs.Properties#generatedemailAddress: PlaceholderResolver.resolveDollarRefs maps '#'->'.' at runtime, resolving Properties.generatedemailAddress.
accepted_dollar_refs.get_partner_account#Respons['accountID']: ReadyAPI source TYPO: the ref is written `#Respons['accountID']` -- missing the `e` and the `#$` separator, so it is not a valid ${step#Response#path} ref. ReadyAPI cannot resolve it either. Report to the suite owner; the converter correctly leaves it literal rather than guessing.

accepted_placeholders.JDBC_validate_otp_after_request_Response: OPEN GAP (1x, post_confirm_validation template): a JDBC step's response column referenced from a request body; the JDBC result is not published under this key.
accepted_placeholders.Request: Javadoc/comment text describing SoapUI ref syntax.
accepted_placeholders.Response: Javadoc/comment text describing SoapUI ref syntax.
accepted_placeholders.ResponseAsXml: Javadoc in RestUtilities describing SoapUI ref syntax, not an emitted placeholder.
accepted_placeholders.olderDate: Groovy local computed in the same translated block; not a cross-step value.
accepted_placeholders.placeholder: Literal word in a Db.java message string.
accepted_placeholders.qry_http_request_400_1_name: SalesforceAuth documents #qry_...# as an intentional mapJsonValues fallback marker.
accepted_placeholders.testcase_inviteKey: OPEN GAP (6x, addmember template): no producer anywhere and the name does not appear in the ReadyAPI XML, so the converter synthesised it. The invite key IS captured elsewhere as Properties.inviteKey / <step>_Response_inviteKey. Sent to the server literally until mapped.
